claim: >-
  Accepted authority supports feature-local inert declarations plus separate
  feature-owned pure construction factories behind consumer-owned ports.
  Activation remains Product Host lifecycle authority. The common authoring lab
  does not reproduce its claimed activation-factory candidate: it serializes a
  redundant string activationRef, then exercises shared runner-owned factories
  identically for all candidates.
authority:
  accepted:
    - "GM-REQ-002 requires declarations to remain serializable and non-executable: docs/requirements/module-system-v1.md:27-31."
    - "GM-REQ-011 through GM-REQ-014 assign executable loading and activation to Product Hosts, require closed factory dependencies, and distinguish construction from activation: docs/requirements/module-system-v1.md:91-119."
    - "ADR-0001 limits Core to inert composition and leaves loading, authorization, lifecycle, and readiness to products: docs/decisions/0001-product-neutral-deterministic-module-composition.md:28-48."
    - "ADR-0004 states that V1 accepts no factories, invokes no product code, and treats dependency order as graph data rather than lifecycle instruction: docs/decisions/0004-freeze-v1-portable-composition-contract-and-plan-digest.md:77-111."
    - "ADR-0008 requires owner-local ports, pure factories, inert declarations, consumer-owned ports, and closed typed dependencies: docs/decisions/0008-bounded-internal-engine-self-composition.md:100-143."
  proposedOnly:
    - "ADR-0010 proposes feature-owned adapters and ordinary TypeScript factories but is not accepted: docs/decisions/0010-select-replaceable-primitives-for-the-first-core-implementation.md:33-76."
    - "ADR-0011 proposes null-prototype dependency records and runtime witness wrappers but remains proposed: docs/decisions/0011-define-private-self-composition-evidence-and-release-custody.md:43-69,185-227."
    - "ADR-0016 proposes typed slot-keyed construction records and a static witness; it explicitly remains non-normative until accepted: docs/decisions/0016-close-the-dependency-record-seam-and-construction-witness-for-self-composition.md:47-91."
  qualificationOnly:
    - "The implementation-readiness report is draft research and cannot select an API: research/implementation-readiness/report.md:20-23."
    - "The common lab is disposable and non-authoritative: tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/README.md:1-6."

observedBehavior:
  - >-
    The split candidate exports an ActivationFactory type and serializes
    {declaration, activationRef}; activationRef is merely the implementationId.
    candidate-split.ts defines or imports no executable factory.
  - >-
    During S27 and S28, the runner imports factories.js and invokes the same
    serviceFactory and consumerFactory inside the loop for all three adapters.
    Consequently, those six host-probe cells can pass without exercising a
    split-candidate factory or a declaration-to-factory relationship.
  - >-
    The runner hardcodes filesPerModule to 2 for the split candidate even though
    its measured candidate source contains no external factory and the shared
    factories.js serves every candidate.
  - >-
    The readiness report nevertheless describes the candidate as
    "Declaration + activation factory" and credits it with preserving the Clean
    Architecture boundary.
  - >-
    The report elsewhere correctly limits the fixtures to authoring and typing,
    keeps self-composition conditional, and assigns activation to the future
    Product Host.
applicability: >-
  This is a P2 qualification-evidence defect, not a production runtime defect:
  the report and fixtures are explicitly non-authoritative and no production
  Core exists. It applies whenever the common lab or report table is used to
  compare a separate factory, claim declaration/factory congruence, or infer a
  files-per-module cost.
benefits:
  - "An inert declaration preserves portability, deterministic compilation, and separation from executable infrastructure."
  - "A separate pure construction factory gives declaration metadata and object construction distinct responsibilities."
  - "Consumer-owned ports and closed dependency arguments preserve dependency inversion and interface segregation."
  - "Co-location within the owning feature preserves DDD ownership without creating a central registry."
  - "Reserving activation for the Product Host prevents Core from becoming a second lifecycle authority."
failureModes:
  - "A serialized activationRef can become a second identity authority or string-keyed executable registry."
  - "Declaration slots and a separately typed dependency record can drift unless a construction witness rejects missing, extra, or renamed dependencies."
  - "Calling a construction factory an activation factory invites readiness, publication, retry, or cleanup side effects into a boundary required to remain pure."
  - "Shared host probes can pass while the candidate-specific factory surface is absent."
  - "Hardcoded file metrics undercount the factory implementation and can bias maintenance comparisons."
counterexamples:
  - >-
    The current split candidate passes through the same declaration semantics
    while containing no factory; therefore candidate-scenario success cannot
    establish a factory split.
  - >-
    type-probes.ts checks a standalone ActivationFactory function against a
    handwritten dependency type, but does not relate that type to
    splitDeclaration.slots.
  - >-
    A conforming alternative is already illustrated in the self-composition
    guide: declaration.ts contains inert identity and slot data while factory.ts
    exposes createFeature(deps) using consumer-owned port types.

      report strength to "declaration plus inert reference; separate factory and

openQuestions:
  - >-
    Which accepted successor, ADR-0016 or another design, will make
    declaration-slot and construction-dependency congruence normative? No
    self-composition construction claim is authorized before that decision.
  - >-
    Should a future lab evaluate internal Core feature factories, product-owned
    adapter factories, or separate lanes for both? Their owners differ even
    though the current "activation factory" label conflates them.
confidence: high
recommendedDecision: >-
  Retain the accepted boundary as the evaluation baseline: feature-local inert
  declaration data, a separate co-located pure construction factory typed only
  to consumer-owned ports, and Product Host-owned activation. Do not serialize
  an activationRef, expose a factory through the Core compiler contract, or use
  the current common lab as evidence for a factory shape. Keep the exact
  dependency-record and witness representation conditional until an ADR is
  accepted.

  - "Exact-subject evidence from real production adapters demonstrates that the separate factory boundary cannot meet required ownership or maintenance constraints."
  - "The replacement still proves inert serialization, closed dependencies, deterministic compilation, framework independence, and a single Product Host lifecycle authority."
